title: Recipe Card
subject: learning your late mother's handwriting from her recipe cards
caption: Chamber pop led by a Wurlitzer electric piano. Wurlitzer with its natural reed bark and tremolo carrying the main figure, a home upright piano doubling it an octave up, a small string quartet entering under the second chorus, vintage drum kit played with brushes and mic'd minimally with one overhead and a kick mic, round electric bass. Warm, narrow and analogue-saturated, drums close and dry rather than roomy. Warm female voice, conversational and lightly worn, very little processing on it. 88 BPM, F major. Tender and slightly comic, and it does not resolve. No synth pad, no programmed drums, no big belted climax, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - Wurlitzer and upright piano]

[Verse 1]
Index card, grease spot on the corner, blue ink gone brown
"Oven hot. Don't open it. You'll know."
That is the whole instruction. That is the whole recipe.
She wrote it for herself. She never wrote it for me.

[Pre-Chorus]
Her sevens have a line through them
Her g's don't close

[Chorus]
I'm learning my mother's handwriting at thirty-eight
Like a language I heard my whole life and never spoke
Every card is a sentence she only had to half-finish
Because she was always going to be there to say the rest

[Verse 2]
There's one that just says "the good pan"
I do not know which one is the good pan
I have eleven pans and I have tried nine of them
I am not going to find it, and I am going to keep trying

[Chorus - strings enter]
I'm learning my mother's handwriting at thirty-eight
Like a language I heard my whole life and never spoke
Every card is a sentence she only had to half-finish
Because she was always going to be there to say the rest to me

[Outro - Wurlitzer, fading]
Oven hot. Don't open it.
I'll know.
